label: CLOCK_2: any real coordinate strictly increasing along the order of moments
definition: CLOCK_2, any order-preserving real coordinate. A TimeClock on a preordered type of moments is a real-valued reading of the moments that strictly increases along their order (Mathlib StrictMono). The duration from a moment s to a later moment t is reading t - reading s. Examples: FLRW cosmic time; a Newtonian absolute time; the identity on the integers, the reals, the non-negative reals or the positive reals; but equally arctan of integer time (bounded) or the logarithm of positive real time (unbounded below). Not a clock in this sense: a mere ordering with no durations, or a coordinate that runs backwards somewhere. Metric finiteness of a past depends on which clock is chosen; see the CLOCK disambiguation 725f3417-73d0-489f-b8ab-7b2628ff36b7.
note: Analyst framework definition; attribution deferred. The MetricGrimReaper theorems hold for every such clock; the intended reading instantiates it with the privileged clock (CLOCK_1). A strictly monotone real clock exists only for orders that embed in the reals, so every past then has a countable coinitial subset: the countable-coinitiality premise of GrimReaperPatchwork is absorbed into the clock's existence, not eliminated, and times with no real clock (reverse omega_1, the long line, lexicographic R x R) are outside the scope of the results. One clock serves the whole frame: every world of a History shares its order of moments and its clock. A frame whose worlds carry different metrics would need a world-indexed clock, which is not built. No dynamics, curvature or proper time along particular worldlines is encoded.
